result.decision_rationale:
The four focused gates passed, and the corrected evaluator characterizes both tested forms of the unmodified 224949Z row. It can still characterize a row that records a survivor stop, a delivered callback, or conflicting cue identities. Its live and persisted callers also disagree when the retirement timestamp is missing.

## Continuation for Claude

Use one Round7 entry point that reads the settlement and retirement time from the emitted row. Preserve the Round6 reader’s use of the historical phase record and timeline. Reconcile positive stop, callback, playback and identity observations across the snapshots each collector actually emitted. Make malformed required fields produce an unknown or failed verdict without throwing.

Exercise the counterexamples below through the shared entry point using copies of the retained rows and the collector-shaped live fixture. Keep the original native FAILs, the accepted Round6 dispositions and the legitimate stop on the survivor’s own disposal. Reconcile the recovery ledger and supply the existing receipt evidence for the historical accounting. Keep this correction within C1’s code/domain scope, its current enrollment and the shared budget. C3 owns package creation and same-run native qualification.

The collector writes a retirement-frame survivor count, per-sample survivor end times, per-source cue observations and withheld callback timestamps. Several of those observations can contradict a successful verdict without being read.

findings.actual: The Round6 path skips directly to the window-end stop result and request time. It returns characterized for this mutation, although both Round6 collectors emitted the earlier count and used it in their own verdict. Round7 also ignores a positive retirement-frame count if the later count says zero.
findings.blocking_rationale: The reader can accept direct evidence that the survivor received a stop during the protected window.
findings.expected: A positive retirement-frame count must prevent characterization. Round6’s initial zero can be combined with its window-end observations. Round7 additionally requires its explicit through-window count.
findings.requested_correction: Consume the retirement-frame survivor count where emitted and reject contradictory pre-disposal stop evidence, including a recorded stop reason. Preserve the later stop issued by the survivor’s own disposal.
findings.requested_evidence: Show that a positive retirement-frame count refuses on a 202648Z copy and on both 224949Z shapes. Retain the unmodified positive controls and the missing Round7 through-window count control.
findings.title: Honor the survivor stop count recorded in the retirement frame
findings.trigger: On a copy of 202648Z, change only afterOtherRetired.survivorStopAttempts from 0 to 1.

findings.actual: The evaluator checks only the length of callbacksWithheld and projects each window sample to survivorPlayback. It ignores the delivered end in the first case and accepts the placeholder callback in the second. A missing playback property in one sample is also silently skipped when another sample is inactive.
findings.blocking_rationale: The evaluator can establish synthetic callback loss despite a recorded delivery or without a readable withheld callback.
findings.expected: A delivered survivor completion anywhere in the observation window must prevent characterization. Withholding requires a readable callback observation, and a missing native read must remain distinguishable from an observed playback state.
findings.requested_correction: Validate the withheld callback timestamps and the required survivor end and playback fields in the window samples. Preserve the accepted terminal playback rules.
findings.requested_evidence: Exercise a recorded in-window end, an unreadable withheld timestamp and an omitted sample playback property on both 224949Z representations. Keep the original row characterized.
findings.title: Use the recorded window observations when judging callback loss
findings.trigger: Set window[1].survivorEndUtc on a 224949Z copy to its sample timestamp while leaving both terminal ends null. Independently, replace the withheld timestamps with [null] and set the per-sample withheld counts to zero.

findings.actual: The identity checks compare before with the settled other and the two terminal survivor cues. They never compare those IDs with the directly observed retirement-frame cue or the per-source inventory. Both substitutions can return characterized.
findings.blocking_rationale: The verdict can attribute a stop or survival to a cue the same collector explicitly associated with the other source.
findings.expected: An explicit contradiction between the selected identity and the collector’s source or retirement observations must refuse characterization.
findings.requested_correction: Correlate the selected other ID with afterOtherRetired.other and check selected identities against the source-specific observations where that collector emitted them. Keep older collectors on their available evidence.
findings.requested_evidence: On both 224949Z shapes, reject the retirement-frame substitution and a consistent substitution across the survivor’s selected and terminal fields that conflicts with the recorded source.
findings.title: Reject cue IDs that contradict the observed source
findings.trigger: On 224949Z change afterOtherRetired.other.playingId from other ID 622 to survivor ID 586. A second case changes the selected survivor and both terminal survivor IDs to 539, which the row lists only under otherSource.

findings.actual: The live call supplies retiredAt separately, so CallbackLossSettled can still return characterized. The persisted test reader derives the time from the row, substitutes DateTime.MinValue and refuses. The live-shape test also uses that persisted reader, so it misses the caller difference. Both callers index otherRetirementSettled before the evaluator’s type guard, which can throw if that property is a JSON null or scalar.
findings.blocking_rationale: Round7’s verdict can depend on information absent from the row that C3 must later interpret identically.
findings.expected: The live and persisted paths must both refuse a Round7 row missing its required retirement timestamp or readable settlement.
findings.requested_correction: Read the Round7 retirement timestamp and settled cue safely inside the same row-based evaluator entry point for both callers. Keep the external phase cue and timeline inputs for the Round6 collectors that need them.
findings.requested_evidence: Use that entry point for both shapes and show equivalent refusals for omitted or unreadable otherRetiredUtc and null or scalar otherRetirementSettled. Retain the recorded no-overlap disposition.
findings.title: Derive the Round7 verdict from the same row in both callers
findings.trigger: Remove otherRetiredUtc from a 224949Z copy and evaluate it with the original local retiredAt value, as the live caller does.

findings.actual: ExplicitNull returns true for JTokenType.Undefined. Unset consequently accepts the terminal field and the otherwise valid row characterizes. Conversely, an object in an end-time field is labeled as a recorded end even though it cannot be read as a timestamp.
findings.blocking_rationale: An unreadable required property can serve as affirmative evidence that no callback occurred.
findings.expected: Only the collector’s explicit null encodings should establish an unset stop or end. An undefined or incompatible value should produce an unreadable-field verdict.
findings.requested_correction: Distinguish JSON null and the collector’s null-valued String JValue from undefined and invalid field types. Keep unreadable values distinct from real stop or completion observations.
findings.requested_evidence: Exercise undefined and wrong-type stop/end fields alongside absent properties, JSON nulls and String-typed nulls.
findings.title: Keep undefined stop and end fields out of the explicit-null case
findings.trigger: Replace survivorAfterDisposal.cue.endUtc on an otherwise valid row with JValue.CreateUndefined().

findings.actual: Number casts any integer token directly to Int32. Id similarly casts to Int64 before checking the UInt32 range. An out-of-range integer can throw OverflowException and abort evaluation.
findings.blocking_rationale: The required invalid-ID and unreadable-count paths must return a verdict the caller can record.
findings.expected: An unrepresentable count or playing ID should produce a failed or unknown verdict.
findings.requested_correction: Check numeric representability before narrowing counts and playing IDs, and return an unreadable result on conversion failure.
findings.requested_evidence: Pass an integer above Int32.MaxValue as the survivor count and an unsigned integer above Int64.MaxValue as a playing ID. Both evaluations should return a refusal without throwing.
findings.title: Handle out-of-range integer observations without aborting the reader
